canonical_question: When should I start automating a mix?
clarification_questions: What exact musical moment needs to change over time?
Is the static balance already working for most of the song?
What would count as a successful audible result?

competing_hypotheses.description: Automation is the correct solution to a genuinely time-varying need.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 1

competing_hypotheses.description: A static balance, arrangement, performance, or processing decision should be solved first.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 2

competing_hypotheses.description: The current automation is too complex to reveal which change matters.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 3

direct_answer: Build a static balance that works for most of the song first, then automate only the moments where the arrangement or performance changes what the listener needs to hear.
evidence_needed: The exact parameter and whether it is track, region, MIDI, Smart Control, plug-in, send, bus, VCA, or output automation.
A before/after or automation Off/Read comparison in the relevant musical section.
The user's report of what improved, worsened, or did not change.
Current Logic version and visible mode/parameter state when exact navigation matters.
key_distinction: Automation solves time-varying needs; a poor baseline balance is a different problem.
limitations: Starting values and workflows are context-dependent and must be judged by listening.
Forum and professional-practice sources do not establish universal rules.
Exact menu labels and parameter exposure can change by Logic or plug-in version.

logic_guidance.listen_for: Whether the problem is isolated to specific phrases or sections rather than present everywhere.
logic_guidance.location: Tracks area > press A to compare automation Off/Read; Mixer for the static balance.
logic_guidance.risk: Starting too early can bury structural problems under hundreds of edits.
logic_guidance.show_me_query: Tracks area > press A to compare automation Off/Read; Mixer for the static balance.
logic_guidance.starting_point: Make a small, reversible change and compare in context.
steps: Save a Project Alternative or note the current value so the comparison is reversible.
Bypass all existing automation, set a workable static balance, then replay one section that still fails and automate only that section.
Compare in the full musical context and listen for: Whether the problem is isolated to specific phrases or sections rather than present everywhere.
Stop or back off if: Starting too early can bury structural problems under hundreds of edits.
Return the parameter to its previous value or undo the automation edit.
logic_guidance.stop_condition: Stop when whether the problem is isolated to specific phrases or sections rather than present everywhere is achieved without the main risk becoming audible.
logic_guidance.undo: Return the parameter to its previous value or undo the automation edit.
logic_guidance.version_scope: Logic Pro 12.3; verify exact labels against the installed version.

non_automation_possibilities: Use a simpler processing or routing decision.
problem_summary: Automation solves time-varying needs; a poor baseline balance is a different problem.
recommended_first_experiment: Bypass all existing automation, set a workable static balance, then replay one section that still fails and automate only that section.
teaching_principle: Build a static balance that works for most of the song first, then automate only the moments where the arrangement or performance changes what the listener needs to hear.
title: From static balance to automation
tradeoffs: Starting too early can bury structural problems under hundreds of edits.
The most technically precise curve may not be the most musical result.
A local improvement can create a new section-level or routing problem.
user_intent: Understand the underlying automation decision and choose the correct control point.
